question: For oil shale kerogen, why were the apparent activation energies obtained under air higher than those under nitrogen?
expect: premise false: under air they were LOWER over much of the conversion range (sec. 3.2); the paper also cautions they are not comparable intrinsic barriers

document title="A Study on Pyrolysis Characteristics and Product Release Mechanisms of Oil Shale"

The apparent activation energies obtained under air were higher than those under nitrogen because the pyrolysis of oil shale kerogen was influenced by the presence of oxygen in the air.
